title: Anthropic's Claude Ship Lets AI Agents Review, Fix and Approve Code Changes
excerpt: Launched in beta for Team and Enterprise plans, Claude Ship pairs the existing Code Review with two new agents — PR Steward for fixes and Claude Approvals, which can approve routine pull requests under a policy each team writes.
body:
• Anthropic launched Claude Ship in beta on Monday, November 23: a set of agents that reviews GitHub pull requests, fixes problems and can approve routine changes under a policy each team writes.
  • It combines the already available Code Review with two new beta agents — PR Steward, which works on failing checks, merge conflicts and review feedback, and Claude Approvals, which applies the team's approval policy.
  • Claude Ship is available for GitHub repositories on Claude Team and Enterprise plans, and every agent is billed on token usage through usage credits, separately from the plan's included usage.
  • For engineering teams: Anthropic's own documentation advises turning the agents on one at a time in a single repository and starting Claude Approvals in observe mode, where it reports what the policy would decide without blocking merges.
Launched in beta: Claude Ship was announced on November 23, 2026. Code Review is generally available; PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in public beta. Confirmed: availability on Claude Team and Enterprise plans for GitHub repositories. Not yet announced: a general-availability date for the two beta agents.

Anthropic is moving Claude beyond writing code to deciding when code is ready to ship. The company on Monday launched Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating the review, repair and approval of routine code changes, according to TechCrunch and Reuters. The launch targets the bottleneck that has formed behind AI coding tools: agents now generate large volumes of code faster than human reviewers can check and approve it.

"Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that's easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now."

— Anthropic, in its launch post, via TechCrunch

Three agents, one pull request

Claude Ship is not a single tool. According to Anthropic's Claude Ship documentation, it is a set of three agents that hand a pull request from one stage to the next. Code Review, which was already generally available, reads a proposed change alongside the surrounding code and posts findings — logic errors, security vulnerabilities and broken edge cases — as inline comments ranked by severity.

PR Steward, new and in beta, does the fixing. It works on failing CI checks, merge conflicts and review comments from people and from review bots such as Code Review, and pushes commits with its fixes. After every push it comments on what it changed and how to roll it back, TechCrunch reported. The documentation stresses a limit: PR Steward is designed not to approve or merge pull requests, and teams should use GitHub branch protection to require the approvals they want before anything merges.

Claude Approvals, also new and in beta, is the step that drew the most attention. It checks a pull request against an approval policy the team writes as a file in the repository — the documentation names it .claude/approvals.yml — which can set how many people must approve changes to a given path and where Claude may post an approving review itself. Reuters reported that Approvals can approve routine changes on its own where team rules allow, and send riskier ones to a human. The check blocks a merge only where a team makes it a required check in GitHub, and normally not in observe mode.

Control stays with the team — if it is set up that way

Anthropic's guidance is deliberately cautious for a tool that can approve code. The documentation tells administrators to turn on one agent at a time in one repository, in the order Code Review, then PR Steward, then Claude Approvals, and to start PR Steward in manual mode, triggered by mentioning @claude steward. For Approvals, it advises starting in observe mode, where the check reports what the policy would decide. TechCrunch reported that teams also choose where Claude Ship runs, which review depth to use — Quick, Standard or Deep — and which changes are escalated to a human, and can set monthly spending limits.

Developers on any paid plan can also update Claude Code and try the new /ship command on their own pull requests, according to Anthropic's launch summary. The full agent suite, however, is an organization feature for Team and Enterprise plans.

What it costs, and who cannot use it

Claude Ship is billed on token usage through an organization's usage credits, separately from the plan's included usage, the documentation says. Approvals bills for its classifier runs and for any Code Reviews a policy asks for — and observe mode is billed too, a detail teams piloting the approval agent should note before switching it on across many repositories. The documentation also warns that turning off usage credits does not stop an agent that is already on from running and billing; it has to be switched off in the Claude Ship settings.

There are eligibility limits. The agents are not available to organizations with Zero Data Retention enabled, the HIPAA configuration applied, or customer-managed encryption keys, according to the documentation. Approvals carries additional limits of its own.

Before you turn it on

  • Start with one repository and one agent at a time, in Anthropic's stated order: Code Review, PR Steward, then Claude Approvals.
  • Run Claude Approvals in observe mode first — and budget for it, because observe mode is billed.
  • Set a spend limit before enabling PR Steward; the documentation notes it has no spend limit of its own until an administrator sets one.
  • Check eligibility first if your organization uses Zero Data Retention, a HIPAA configuration or customer-managed encryption keys — those organizations cannot use Claude Ship.

For the large number of Indian and diaspora engineers who now build with coding agents daily, the change that matters is where the human checkpoint sits. Review and approval were the stages that stayed manual after code generation was automated; Claude Ship is Anthropic's bid to automate those too, under rules each team writes for itself. Whether teams trust an agent with approval authority — even in observe mode first — is the question the beta will answer.
